issues.description: Removing the outer Delimited around ALTER TABLE actions silently regresses comma-chained multi-action statements.
issues.detail: The old grammar wrapped actions in Delimited(OneOf(...)), accepting e.g. `ALTER TABLE t ADD col ..., DROP COLUMN x`. The new bare OneOf permits exactly one action, and the load-bearing fixture demonstrating that form was deleted with no citation that it is invalid T-SQL. Either restore comma-chained actions or document the deliberate scope reduction with a spec reference.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar admits an optional sign on the increment with no stated invariant or negative/boundary tests.
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is now optional before both seed and increment numeric literals. T-SQL's increment must be a non-zero integer, and no fixture exercises a negative increment or rejects pathological cases like `+1, -0` or double signs. Either tighten the grammar to the seed (or to a single signed-numeric-literal rule) or add a comment stating that semantic validation is deferred.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no fixture, no citation, and no justification in the PR description.
issues.detail: The OneOf was widened to include numeric literals (presumably LCID), but no test exercises the numeric branch and the PR description does not mention it. Either add a fixture like `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033` with a comment citing the LCID case, or drop the alternative. Untested speculative grammar branches should not ship.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN/DROP CONSTRAINT branches use a nested Delimited(Sequence(...)) shape that admits ambiguous mixed forms.
issues.detail: The inner Sequence makes `COLUMN`/`CONSTRAINT` optional per item, so `DROP COLUMN a, b, COLUMN c` and `DROP CONSTRAINT a, b, CONSTRAINT c` parse. Pick one shape per T-SQL spec — either one keyword with a delimited reference list, or a repeated `KEYWORD ref` per item — and split into named sub-grammars. The current shape also erodes the structural distinction between column and constraint drops.

issues.description: Four unrelated grammar changes are bundled into one patch, harming bisectability.
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN identifiers, signed IDENTITY seed, and the ALTER TABLE DROP refactor are independent features touching different segments. Splitting into separate commits would let each land, revert, or bisect on its own merits and would force per-change justification of the spec changes.

issues.description: AlterTableStatementSegment is a sprawling OneOf that should decompose into named per-action sub-grammars.
issues.detail: The ~12 sibling sequences form a keyword-dispatched table (ADD/DROP/ALTER/SET/REBUILD/RENAME). Lifting each branch to a named grammar (AlterTableAddSegment, AlterTableDropSegment, etc.) would make the structure self-evident, allow downstream rules to dispatch by named subtype rather than lookahead, and make each branch independently testable.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly on three P1 concerns: the ALTER TABLE refactor silently narrows the grammar by dropping the outer Delimited (and the deleted fixture is the evidence), the IDENTITY seed/increment grammar admits a sign on both positions without stated invariants or boundary tests, and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE was widened to numeric literals with no fixture or citation. Secondary concerns are structural: the nested Delimited(Sequence) shape for DROP branches admits ambiguous mixed surface forms and erodes the column-vs-constraint distinction, and the monolithic AlterTable OneOf should decompose into named per-action grammars. The PR also bundles four independent features into one patch. NEEDS-WORK: restore or justify multi-action ALTER TABLE, tighten and test the IDENTITY and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE additions, and split the patch.
